paper_metadata.title: Effects of solution aging treatments on microstructure features, tensile properties and low-cycle fatigue behavior of Ti-6.2Al-4.26Mo-1.33Mn alloy

evidence.quote: This work developed a high-elastic-modulus Ti-6.2Al-4.26Mo-1.33Mn alloy with good balance of strength and plasticity through regulating its primary equiaxed α ( α p ) phase with solution aging treatment.
In this work, the effects of solution aging treatment on αp phase, tensile properties and LCF behavior of pre-developed high elastic modulus Ti-6.2Al-4.26Mo-1.33Mn alloy were systematically studied.

10 KG ingot with chemical composition Ti-6.2Al-4.26Mo-1.33Mn (wt.%) was prepared by vacuum induction suspension melting with water-colded copper crucible.
The ingot was forged into a bar with a diameter of 20 mm at temperatures in the range of 900 – 950 ◦ C
The solution treatment was carried out at 825 – 925 ◦ C for 1h, and water cooling (WC) was carried out immediately after the solution was completed.
Then aging at 550 ◦ C for 4 h and air cooling (AC).

conditions.test_method: DMA 850 dynamic mechanical analysis, single cantilever fixture, stress amplitude 600 MPa, frequency 5 Hz

evidence.quote: Under the conditions of T = 35 ◦ C, f = 5 Hz and σ a = 600 MPa, the LCF experiment shows that the number of fatigue failure cycles of the alloy increases significantly with the increase of solution temperature

evidence.section: 4.2. Effect of solution temperature on the tensile properties

evidence.quote: Moreover, the fatigue performance is also significantly improved, which is associated with the reduced α p phase that was characterized to act as crack initiations and crack propagation path.

It has been reported that the α phase is mainly strengthened by solution hardening of Al, and the enrichment of Al increases with increasing solution temperature, and the hardness of the grains also increases [33].

evidence.section: 4.2. Effect of solution temperature on the tensile properties
evidence.quote: In addition, αs phase will precipitate in the βt after aging, resulting in precipitation strengthening, so the hardness of the sample will increase with the increase of solution temperature.

the αs phase can hinder the movement of dislocations during the deformation process, resulting in the formation of a high-density dislocation accumulation area at the interface between the soft phase αp and the hard phase αs. The stress concentration at the boundary of αp and αs phase leads to the initiation of cracks.

the higher the solution temperature, the lower the number of dislocations exist in the αp phase. Under the action of fatigue load, there will be less dislocation slip towards the interface of the αp phase and the αs phase, resulting in a longer time to form a high-density dislocation accumulation zone, so the fatigue life is longer.
